# Fanfarr v0.5.0

Fanfarr finds theme music for a Plex library, writes it beside the media as a
local `theme.mp3`, and keeps a permanent record of what it did and why.

## It tells you when something fails

Every scheduled job here runs unattended, and until now the only sign that one
had failed was a badge on a page nobody had open. The failure and the discovery
of it were separated by however long it took somebody to log in.

Point it at a webhook and it will say so. **Pasting the address is the whole of
the setup**: the shape is read from the URL, so `discord.com` is Discord,
`hooks.slack.com` is Slack, `gotify` in the host is Gotify, `ntfy` in the host is
ntfy, and anything else is sent as plain text -- which a dumb receiver
understands, where JSON needs a parser written for it on the far end.

**Four kinds of event, each with its own switch.** A job that runs out of
retries, a health check on the way into failure, a backup that could not be
written, and a library sync finishing. The failures are on by default; the
routine one is off, because a sync that finishes every six hours is noise to most
people and exactly what somebody else wants.

**Send a test** on the Notifications card ignores the switches: the point of it
is to find out whether the URL and the shape are right.

Three rules keep it from being a nuisance:

- **A health check notifies on the transition**, not on every run that finds it
  still broken. An appliance that repeats itself is one people stop reading.
- **A job notifies when it runs out of retries**, not on every attempt, so a job
  that fails and is retried does not announce itself five times.
- **Delivery is best-effort.** A timeout or a 500 is logged and swallowed: a job
  that did its work and then failed because the notification *about* it could not
  be delivered would be worse than silence.

Nothing is sent until a URL is set, so this changes nothing on upgrade.

## Fixed: a release that had a tag and no image

v0.4.0's image was never built. The version-bump job's push was rejected because
another commit landed while it was running, and since a push made with
`GITHUB_TOKEN` starts no workflow of its own, the bump commit that followed built
nothing either -- leaving a tag, a release, and no image to pull.

The bump now retries from the current tip, so the only way to lose is somebody
pushing in the seconds between the fetch and the push, which is what the retry is
for.

## Also

- The build now publishes an SBOM and provenance alongside the image.
- Workflow values reach the scripts through the environment rather than being
  interpolated into them: a branch name can contain shell metacharacters, and
  `${{ }}` inside a `run:` block is how that becomes code.

## Upgrading

Pull the new image and restart; the database migrates itself on boot. One thing
worth knowing:

- **Notifications are off until you set a webhook URL.** Nothing is sent, and
  nothing changes, until then. Settings > Notifications has the URL, the shape,
  the switches, and a test button.
